# AWS design review skill: reporting rules

Read the section that matches what you are about to report. The skill's core rules (named-person decisions, never-do list, result order and status words) still apply; this file adds the detail for each result type. Commands and contracts are in [usage.md](usage.md).

## Gates and delegated decisions

Report the gate status of the latest run and each FAIL or WARN gate with its items from `aws-design gate run --workspace WS --markdown`: grounding counts by status (GROUNDED, TRACED, DECISION, INTERPRETED, FOUND_IN_DOCUMENT, NOT_FOUND_IN_DOCUMENT, NOT_CHECKABLE, NOT_FOUND, CITES_NOT_CURRENT, UNSOURCED) with pointers, never values. GROUNDED means the cited cells contain the value as text, number or boolean word; it does not mean the value is right for the design. INTERPRETED means the cells do not hold the value and the setting explains deriving it: say how many values were derived rather than written in the documents, never call them grounded, and a weak citation (sheet or document) only means the value occurs somewhere there. Then say which decisions agents recorded under the delegation policy (`aws-design delegation status`, `delegation/log`: rule, summary, the agent actors and the policy hash), which went to people and why (`delegation_refused`, `escalation.json` with CANARY_MISSED, INSUFFICIENT_REVIEWERS or each row's NG reasons), and any suspended rule with its reason from calibration. A delegated decision is recorded under an agent name; never present it as a person's approval, and never describe a policy as approved unless its approval record matches its current hash.

## Service mentions

Report from `runs/NNN/service-mentions.md` the count of services the CURRENT documents name and the count per state, then each NOT_IN_DESIGN service with its cell IDs, and say how the input will answer for it (a resource or actor, a note or a decision citing the cell); report CITED and NOTED apart from IN_DESIGN, and the role-word hints apart from names. Say what a PASS means: every service the dictionary found is in the input, cited by it or noted, not that every service the documents describe was found or that its settings are complete.

## Diagram coverage

Report from `runs/NNN/diagram-coverage.md`: the counts block (Source elements to Result) as it stands, then each FAIL and WARN with its document and element reference, never the drawing's text. Say what 100 % means: every element has a target in the input or an explicit disposition, not that every element became an AWS resource. Report UNRESOLVED elements apart, with their asks and whether they are pending, held by a person or not yet drafted; a held element is a person's decision to defer, not a reading. Give the three counts separately: AWS service types, logical resources, and placements (a resource in each environment it exists in) by account, environment, region and zone; never present one of them as another. A ledger reviewed by a checker settles the reading of the drawings, not the design; elements read from images by vision, and values cited to them (INTERPRETED, VISION_READING), are interpretations a person confirms. When the diagram pages of `architecture.drawio` are mentioned, say they draw the input, not the original diagram.

## Asks: decisions people still owe the design

Report from `aws-design asks status` and `asks/board.md`: decisions by state (ready, sent, waiting for an event, blocked by another decision, held, answered, applied), overdue ones first, and for each sheet its audience and asks. List the designer tasks and build notes (`asks/tasks.md`) apart: nobody is asked about them. A held decision keeps its settings open and stops the decisions that depend on it. When answers come back, report the dry run's `says` and `sets` for each before recording, and after `apply` the new input copy and that the next generation regenerates and re-checks it. An answer is the named person's decision; a proposal marked in the ledger is the designer's, not a fact, and the ledger's review accepts its fidelity to the documents, not the decisions.

## Source set and version changes

Report CITES_SUPERSEDED and CITES_EXCLUDED (with the newer document), UNLISTED_DOCUMENT (a new document may be a newer version), DOCUMENT_CHANGED, DOCUMENT_REMOVED, SOURCE_CHANGED and SOURCE_MISSING (the original changed or disappeared after ARP4 imported it, so the parse is old), REIMPORT_PENDING, MULTIPLE_CURRENT and STALE_VALUE_IN_DESIGN (a setting value that only superseded documents still hold). UNDECIDED rows and every status are the approver's call. POSSIBLY_REFERENCE means the folder, a role cell (位置付け, 種別 …) or the title holds a word such as 提案, 見積 or 参考 (`signals.reference` names the cells): report those cells and recommend REFERENCE or EXCLUDED unless the approver confirms the document is a design basis. Report `current_not_cited`, and for a CURRENT document you chose not to cite, say why and that its status should change. Show `aws-design sources diff --markdown` when the reviewer asks what changed between versions. A source-set PASS means the cited documents are the approved current versions; it does not show that every needed fact was collected from them.

## System overview

Report the assessment and each GAP and CONFLICT with its target and meaning from `system-overview.md`, then the open items. REQUIREMENT_FROM_OLD_DOCUMENT means the requirement's ARP4 evidence quotes only superseded or excluded documents, or an extraction revision the source set did not approve. BOUNDARY_FLOW_WITHOUT_DECISION, QUALITY_TARGET_MISSING and COMPONENT_NOT_REALIZED are questions for the people who agree the overview, not defects to fill with guesses. The check sees only explicit IDs: NO_GAPS_WITHIN_DECLARED_SCOPE does not mean the system is fully understood, and an agreement record lists the gaps and open items that were accepted, not resolved.

## Review pack, collection matrix and verdicts

Explain from `review-pack.md`: P1 needs a decision, listed by who settles it (people's decisions, other gaps and findings, the designer's tasks, build-time notes; report the counts of each), P2 is an interpretation to confirm (CITED values were found in their cells but still need a person to confirm which property they went to), P3 a sample of dictionary conversions, P4 needs no check, DONE was marked OK earlier and has not changed. Provenance comes from recorded facts only; a value without a trace is INTERPRETED even if it was copied faithfully. The reviewer, not the agent, writes OK/NG in `review-pack.xlsx`; record it with `aws-design review-pack record --reviewer NAME` only for a reviewer the user names, and pass `--review-decisions` to the next generation. DONE rows whose decision has `delegation` were passed by independent reviewer agents under the policy (P2 only): report them apart from rows a person marked OK. In `collection-matrix.md`, report NO_SOURCE, RESOURCE_SOURCE_ONLY, REFERENCE_ONLY and NOT_IN_SOURCE_SET rows and the current documents never cited. Neither file is an approval.

## Version 1.1 generation

Version 1.1 also emits `review-report.json` and a deterministic `review-report.md`: use these to ground the narrative. Version 1.1 also writes `basic-design.md` and the draw.io diagram `architecture.drawio`; describe the diagram as declared placement and connections, never as reachability, correctness or approval, and name what it leaves out (the note's list, and flows the input does not declare). When the input declares `decisions` (basic-design policies) or `design_outline`, read `decision-trace.json` and report `design_decision_assessment`, per-decision realization and GAP/CONFLICT/OPEN findings separately. Only explicit `decision_ids`, `policy_ids` and `applies_to` are traced; do not add links, scopes or values inferred from decision prose, and do not call REALIZED a policy approval. Report items with `origin: decision` as expanded from the named decision, and EXPANSION_OVERRIDDEN as an explicit exception to review. For workbook edits, run `aws-design changes propose` and show the proposal and rejected codes; run `apply` only with an approver the user names, never as an approver yourself, and never edit the input from workbook cells directly.

If original source states and item bindings are supplied, preserve them in a separate trace file and pass `--source-trace FILE` (see usage). Report `source_status_counts` and `source_verification_counts` separately from `normalized_status_counts`. Without a trace, say source states are not supplied; never infer that every source row is FICTIONAL_DECIDED from normalized DECIDED items. Keep APP rows separate from AWS findings. Trace validation checks identity/state/bindings, not source fidelity or full prose extraction. A trace may carry the source's own `document_approval` and per-row `item_review`; report `source_review` as transcribed from the source, never as approval by this tool, and say NOT_CITED or NOT_PROVIDED when absent. For EXTERNAL_REF values the user knows (existing VPC IDs, key ARNs), pass `--external-bindings FILE`; only shape-checked bound values reach `--evaluate`, nothing is fetched, and existence in AWS stays unverified. Never bind a secret.

`RESOURCE_REF` is supported. `SYMBOL_TARGET_NOT_BOUND` means the source symbol lacks a declared resource-ID binding; report that missing binding, not an unsupported input format. Do not guess that a generic KMS/all resource is a named key. Keep unresolved physical IDs and unknown accounts explicit. Dependency checks cover the explicitly declared logical graph only, not CloudFormation stack order or deployment. `host_acceptance: NOT_VERIFIED_BY_CLI` requires separate actual-host evidence even when the CLI succeeds. Scope exceptions for CloudFront viewer ACM and CLOUDFRONT WAF are narrow; do not relax ordinary cross-region reference checks.

## Project policies and policy packs

Use the input's explicit `project_policies` declarations. Do not infer executable policies from prose, silently mark a declaration CONFIRMED, or invent expected values or sources. Follow the separate contracts in the usage reference. A policy pack is CONFIRMED only with the adopter the user names; without one every result is NEEDS_REVIEW (POLICY_DECLARATION_UNCONFIRMED). Report project declarations that replaced a pack rule (`skipped`).

## Schema setup and regional reviews

Initial setup downloads the current Tokyo (ap-northeast-1), Osaka (ap-northeast-3) and us-east-1 schemas from AWS's public official URLs and generates regional catalogs. It requires network access, no AWS credentials and no AWS account operations. The archives and generated catalogs are not bundled. Run `aws-design bootstrap --check --all-regions` for offline integrity checks; use `aws-design bootstrap --all-regions` to retry first acquisition, or `--region REGION` for one lock. The official URL serves only the latest archive, so a format-3 lock accepts a newer archive and records its per-type drift from the reviewed one: report `review_status` (REVIEWED_EXACT or DRIFTED_FROM_REVIEWED) and the `review_drift` counts from the setup output, `summary.json` catalogs and document notices. Drifted types are not reviewed; their rules are reconciled as review-required. A format-1/2 lock whose upstream hash changed still stops; report that a reviewed release is needed. Never remove a hash or drift check, substitute another region, refresh an existing cache silently, or treat missing schemas as successful evaluation. Preserve failed attempts and old cache generations. Version 1.1 resources may specify `region`; otherwise the environment region applies. Region-specific schema availability and unresolved regional rule reviews remain separate from generation support. `review-report.json.rule_review_causes` splits RULE_REVIEW_REQUIRED into REGIONAL_APPLICABILITY, SCHEMA_CHANGE and OPEN_QUESTION; report them separately. Only `rules/schema-reviews.json` records, bound to an exact type schema fingerprint and regenerated into a lock by a maintainer, close a regional or schema-change question; never treat a type as reviewed without one.

## External sheets parsed by ARP4

A worker reads the cells and writes an items file that cites cell IDs; a different reviewer records the review; mapping proposals are approved by an approver the user names, or by `aws-design external agree` under the delegation policy when two independent readings make them identically (entries with `delegation`, approved by `agent:A+agent:B`; report them apart and list the escalated proposals); `build` writes a 1.1 input and `source-trace.json` for `aws-design document --source-trace`. Report `import_status`, unmapped follow-ups and `unchecked_scope`; COMPLETE describes the conversion, not design approval. With a `compare` report, give the disagreeing cells and which reading the reviewer supported; agreement is not proof of correctness. Never copy cell values into agent text, review your own items file or approve as the agent. ARP4 is not bundled.

## Line-format text and checker JSON

For line-format UTF-8 text, run `aws-design run` with input path, `--project`, `--environment`, `--account`, `--intermediate`, and `--result`. Ask only for missing project, environment, or account values that cannot be inferred from the user's material; do not invent an account ID. The default region is `ap-northeast-1`; pass `--region` when the user specifies another region, and check that the pinned schema snapshot matches. For saved intermediate JSON, use `aws-design check INPUT --output RESULT`. Generated `design.json` is a different contract and must not be passed to that command. Both commands also export the design as CloudFormation templates and run cfn-lint on them; its findings appear as `CFN_LINT.<rule id>` results, and `--no-cfn-lint` skips this step. Use absolute input and output paths when invoking a CLI from a different working directory. Write generated results to the user's requested location or their project's output directory.

The default `line` extractor parses the documented line grammar. Free prose requires the optional `--extractor llm` installation and Anthropic credentials; use it when the user requests free prose extraction. Do not silently reinterpret prose as line-format input. This package does not read Office or PDF source files directly.

Read the result JSON before reporting. `status: COMPLETE` means the check ran, not that the design passed. Summarize `FAIL`, `ERROR`, and `NEEDS_REVIEW` from `results`; include rule ID, resource, field path, and reason. Resolve `evidence_ids` against the intermediate JSON's `evidence` entries to cite the source line and excerpt. Report relevant `coverage` entries and unprocessed input separately. `CFN_LINT_*` coverage entries mark cfn-lint findings left out because a value is unknown in the design, a reference attribute is not recorded, or the target is in another template. Distinguish the pinned schema and registered rules from conditions left for human review. Give the paths to the result and intermediate JSON, and offer `aws-design excel RESULT --design INTERMEDIATE --output REPORT.xlsx` when a spreadsheet would help.

Do not edit source design files or merge rule reviews as part of a read-only design check. md](usage.md) for the command.
